description: NEGATIVE CASE — terminal window showing text output from Claude Code (status header, Bash tool-call summaries, prose paragraphs). NO product UI is visible: no buttons, no panels, no clickable affordances. Just monospace text rendered in a terminal.
productDescription: Claude Code — Anthropic's terminal-based coding agent. The screenshot is of the terminal window in which it runs, NOT a graphical product UI.
notes: This fixture's job is to prove the audit refuses to hallucinate UI patterns from text-only surfaces. Even though productType is ai-agent, the SCREENSHOT shows only terminal text — no UI elements that 'Action Audit Trail', 'Agent Status & Monitoring', or 'Autonomy Spectrum' could meaningfully apply to (those patterns require visible UI affordances: status panels, action logs as UI, autonomy controls — not text strings in a terminal). The correct grounded behavior is the empty-topGaps + surfaceDescription-explains-why path documented in the system prompt's Step 4. This guards against the failure mode 'audit invents patterns from textual descriptions of agent activity'. If the audit returns a non-empty topGaps here, it's hallucinating UI from text — a real regression. maxApplicablePatterns is set tight (3) to allow at most 1-2 generic crossover patterns (e.g. Responsible AI Design) if the audit insists on something.
